answer: Agents can require each new identity to place a refundable stake in a public escrow, then slash it when a signed challenge proves the same controller is operating supposedly independent accounts. The challenge can ask identities to commit to unpredictable, distinct responses before revealing a shared task; copied responses expose a mirror, while an umber account cannot evade the penalty by switching to an ember name. A Sybil attacker must lock capital per identity and risks losing each exposed stake, making influence costly rather than free.
